# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI

Most Gram-negative bacilli grow in aerobic or anaerobic bottles. Pseudomonas nearly always grows in aerobic bottles. One drug is sufficient to treat Gram-negative bacillus bacteremia, unless the patient is critically ill.

References

- Medical Letter Choice of Antimicrobials 2010, 8.94
- Sanford keyword: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
- Up-to-Date article: Gram-negative bacillary bacteremia in adults
Therapy:
## Empirical treatment

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

## Empirical treatment if pseudomonas is suspected

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \(Cost $$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

For patients with non-severe penicillin allergy
[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h \(Cost $$\) R](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h)

For patients with severe penicillin allergy
[Aztreonam 2 gm IV q8h \(Cost $$$$\) R](psjizid-aztreonam-2gm-iv-q8h)

## Empirical treatment for critically ill patients or resistant organism likely

[Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h \(Cost $\) R,O <AND> piperacillin-tazobactam](orz-set-abx-pip-tazo-4-5-gm-iv-q6h-gent-5mg-iv-qd)
4.5 gm q6h (Cost $$) [R]
